newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-FORMER CHAMPION PIERCE THROUGH TO FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-FORMER CHAMPION PIERCE THROUGH TO FINAL.

text.p: Former champion Mary Pierce earned a place in the finals of the Australian Open on Thursday, beating in-form South African Amanda Coetzer in straight sets.
The unseeded Frenchwoman, still a crowd favourite in Melbourne after her victory here in 1995, beat the South African 12th seed 7-5 6-1 in a superbly aggressive tennis display.
Coetzer, 25, ousted world number one Steffi Graf in straight sets in the fourth round of the tournament and had been expected to put up a tougher battle against the Frenchwoman.
Pierce started powerfully, building up a 5-1 lead in the first set only to see Coetzer come back to even the scoreline. She held her serve and broke Coetzer for the set.

Coetzer broke Pierce's serve in the first game of the second but the former champion, dominating at the net and playing at her aggressive best, won the next six games to wrap up the match in 74 minutes.

Pierce's next opponent will be either young Swiss star Martina Hingis, the number four seed, or veteran American Mary Joe Fernandez, seeded 14. Hingis and Fernandez were to play immediately after the first semifinal.
